angle: hd2d-pixel: HD-2D (Octopath / Triangle Strategy / Live A Live / DQ3 HD-2D) and pixel-art-in-3D techniques (t3ssel8r-style post stack, Dead Cells 3D-to-2D sprites, Blender pre-render pipelines), how to replicate them in Three.js r180 with free tools, plus a headless Blender experiment run in this container.

keyFindings.claim: HD-2D is a method on stock Unreal Engine, not a special engine.
keyFindings.detail: DQ3 HD-2D producer Hayasaka: there is no 'HD-2D engine'; you place pixel characters on 3D backgrounds and apply effects. Octopath (UE4) relied heavily on Unreal with a small team.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: The renderer is not the bottleneck. Orbkin's post and light stack is already comparable, so effort should go into authored content.

keyFindings.claim: HD-2D backgrounds are authored 3D models. DQ3 HD-2D dropped pixel textures on backgrounds entirely.
keyFindings.detail: Octopath and Triangle Strategy use low-poly authored geometry with pixel-art textures. OT2 raised map resolution for an 'organic pixel-art appearance'. DQ3 HD-2D uses no pixel art in backgrounds; only characters and monsters are pixels.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: Replace hand-coded procedural boxes with Blender-authored low-poly kit pieces (glTF). Keep the TS texture painters as a texture generator for authored UVs.

keyFindings.claim: In Octopath, VFX spawn point lights so sprites cast shadows onto the 3D world.
keyFindings.detail: Acquire's lead artist Mika Iizuka: plain battle VFX did not look good enough, so a point light was added with each effect, letting characters cast shadows on the environment.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: Attach a short-lived shadow-casting (high tier) or non-shadow point light to each move FX. Sprites already cast real-mesh shadows.

keyFindings.claim: Depth of field is called 'extremely important' to HD-2D by the DQ3 team.
keyFindings.detail: The PlayStation Blog interview credits Horii's comment about background blur. Octopath PC exposes tilt-shift and bloom as separate toggles. Orbkin limits tilt-shift to about 1 px to protect texture crispness.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: Use depth-based blur on the far wall and window only (≤2 px at 640×360, then Bayer-dithered), keeping floor and sprites crisp, instead of a screen-Y tilt band.

keyFindings.claim: Dead Cells pipeline: crude 3D model → keyframed animation → rendered tiny with no AA → PNG plus normal map per frame → toon shading.
keyFindings.detail: Thomas Vasseur, Motion Twin. Character is about 50 px tall in game, so detailed models are cost-inefficient. A homebrew renderer outputs no-AA frames and normal maps, and a cel shader lights them in game.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: For trainers and hero species, pre-render albedo and normal pose sheets in Blender at the in-game texel height, then hand-clean them in Pixelorama.

keyFindings.claim: t3ssel8r-style 3D pixel art uses five parts: low internal resolution, texel-snapped camera with sub-pixel compensation, object snapping, banded lighting, and a depth/normal edge pass.
keyFindings.detail: Read in the code of bababuyyy (Unity, MIT, 640×360 default), denovodavid/David Holland's Godot code via astrellon (MIT), leopeltola (MIT) and three.js RenderPixelatedPass. The silhouette darkens the nearer pixel; convex creases get a highlight on the pixel that faces away more; concave creases get nothing.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: Orbkin has everything except a world-space edge pass, which is the missing piece that makes 3D rock tiers read as drawn pixel art.

keyFindings.claim: three.js r180 ships RenderPixelatedPass with normalEdgeStrength 0.3 and depthEdgeStrength 0.4 defaults, but it re-renders the scene with a MeshNormalMaterial override.
keyFindings.detail: Depth edges come from a 4-neighbour depth difference, floor(smoothstep(.01, .02, diff)*2)/2. Normal edges come from (1 - n·n') gated to the shallower pixel and a bias direction. The output multiplies the beauty colour by (1 - 0.4·dei) or (1 + 0.3·nei). The example also pixel-aligns the frustum and objects.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: Do not drop it in as-is: the override pass breaks custom sprite materials and doubles scene cost (GTAO was rejected for the same reason). Port its indicator logic onto depth-reconstructed normals or an MRT normal target.

keyFindings.claim: A world edge pass can run without a second scene render by reconstructing view position and normals from the depth buffer.
keyFindings.detail: Use 5 depth taps per internal pixel at 640×360. The silhouette threshold scales with linear depth because the camera is perspective. A convex ridge shows as positive second difference of depth.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: P0 change: add an `edges` stage to GradePass (or a new pass) before sprite compositing, behind ?post=edges for A/B, and measure on SwiftShader.

keyFindings.claim: Smooth sub-pixel camera motion comes from snapping the camera and re-adding the snap error as a UV offset at upscale.
keyFindings.detail: denovodavid: snap the position in the camera's rotation frame to the texel size, set h_offset/v_offset, and record texel_error for the output shift. bababuyyy: _PixelPanOffset plus a sharp-bilinear upscale using fwidth/smoothstep at texel borders.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: Optional P3: a final device-resolution blit with the remainder offset smooths intros and shakes and fixes non-integer phone scales.

keyFindings.claim: Camera grid snapping is exact only for orthographic projection.
keyFindings.detail: Texel Splatting (Ebert, arXiv 2603.14587, 2026) and ProPixelizer's author: under perspective the drift rate depends on depth.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: Orbkin's perspective battle camera can only be exact at the focus depth, which it already does. Keep camera moves slow and mostly static during battle.

keyFindings.claim: Headless Blender 5.2.2 (pip bpy) works here. Cycles CPU renders sprite passes in about 10 ms per frame at 128 px.
keyFindings.detail: Albedo and camera-space-normal emission overrides at 1 spp are deterministic, crisp (0 partial-alpha pixels) and noise-free. 8 directions at 128 px took 0.18 s of render (0.9 s wall including import bpy).
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: A tools/blender pipeline can batch-render every species and pose in minutes, in CI or this container, with no GPU.

keyFindings.claim: Multi-sample Cycles does not give binary alpha even with filter_width 0.01 BOX, but 1 spp does.
keyFindings.detail: At 16 spp, 165 partial-alpha edge pixels (multiples of 1/16) remained even with scene.cycles.use_pixel_jitter=False. render.filter_size is EEVEE's setting; Cycles uses scene.cycles.filter_width.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: Render at 1 spp with emission-only passes and do lighting in post or in game, or binarise alpha (threshold 0.5) after rendering.

keyFindings.claim: EEVEE works headless on CPU after installing libEGL (llvmpipe), and the Shader to RGB toon ramp works.
keyFindings.detail: Needs apt-get install libegl1 libegl-mesa0 libgl1-mesa-dri and EGL_PLATFORM=surfaceless. The first frame takes 11–19 s (shader compile), later frames about 1.8–2.7 s at 64 px. filter_size 0.01 with 1 TAA sample gives 0 partial alpha.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: EEVEE toon previews are possible but about 100× slower than Cycles passes on CPU. Prefer Cycles passes and post toon.

keyFindings.claim: Freestyle outlines at sprite resolution (64 px) are anti-aliased and cluttered. A 4-neighbour alpha outline in post reads much better.
keyFindings.detail: With Freestyle on, a CC0 RobotExpressive walk sheet (8 dirs × 4 frames, 64 px) had mushy inner lines and took 89.8 s. Without Freestyle plus a post outline (25–30% of the neighbour colour) it was clean and took 58.8 s.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: Keep Orbkin's own 1-texel outline logic for both live bakes and pre-renders. Do not use Freestyle under ~96 px.

keyFindings.claim: Median-cut palette reduction drops small but distinct colours.
keyFindings.detail: At 16 colours the creature's small cream tail merged into orange. pixel3d-renderer uses OKLab minimax merging so small objects are not absorbed, and Orbkin's extractPalette already keeps rare-but-distinct colours.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: Use Orbkin's palette extractor, or an OKLab minimax variant, in the Blender post step. Never use plain median cut for sprites.

keyFindings.claim: Smooth normal-map lighting on pixel sprites produces too many tones and stops looking like pixel art.
keyFindings.detail: Defold community and arXiv 2212.09692 note that naive normal mapping breaks pixel-art conventions ('Hi-bit'). The fix is quantising lit output into bands and snapping to a palette.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: Pre-rendered normal-mapped billboards must use the same banded ramp and palette snap as the live bake (onBeforeCompile on MeshLambertMaterial, which has normalMap in r180).

keyFindings.claim: Children of Morta lights pixel sprites with high-resolution lights by stretching the pixel art about 4×.
keyFindings.detail: Dead Mage: 'the puppets are pixelated but are lit with real lights'. Lighting resolution is decoupled from art resolution.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: An alternative look: Orbkin chose the opposite (light inside the low-res frame). Keep that, since it matches the crisp reference, but it is a valid A/B.

keyFindings.claim: Sea of Stars' lighting uses a custom render pipeline; no technical breakdown is public.
keyFindings.detail: The press kit promises 'full-on dynamic lighting' through a custom pipeline. Whether sprites use normal maps is unconfirmed.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: Do not base decisions on Sea of Stars specifics. Use the documented t3ssel8r and Dead Cells techniques.

keyFindings.claim: Free tooling covers the whole pipeline, with licence caveats.
keyFindings.detail: Blender (GPL), Pixelorama (MIT), LibreSprite (GPL-2, Aseprite 1.1.8 fork), Aseprite (EULA: self-compile for personal use, no redistribution), Laigter (GPL-3, outputs are yours), and the SpriteSheetMaker and BlenderSpriteGenerator add-ons (MIT). Licences were checked via raw GitHub.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: Standardise on Blender, a headless bpy script and Pixelorama. Optionally build Aseprite locally for personal use.

keyFindings.claim: Most CC0 asset sites are blocked from this container, but GitHub-hosted CC0 assets are reachable.
keyFindings.detail: kenney.nl, polyhaven, ambientcg, quaternius, opengameart, itch and lospec all return proxy-denied. raw.githubusercontent.com works: Kenney starter kits (CC0 assets), the three.js examples/models (RobotExpressive.glb, CC0, downloaded and baked successfully), npm and PyPI.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: Have the owner download CC0 kits locally (free) and commit them under an assets/ folder with licences, or pull them from GitHub mirrors in-container.

keyFindings.claim: Stepped (sprite-like) animation playback makes 3D models read as sprites.
keyFindings.detail: Robert-K's godot-3d-pixel-art lists 'stepped 3D animation playback to emulate spritesheet animation'. Dead Cells keyframes few poses with snappy timing.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: Sample idle and rig motion at 8–12 fps in the live bake (Orbkin already re-bakes at a 'sprite frame rate'; tune it), with big moves kept snappy.

keyFindings.claim: The closest public three.js analogue is pixel3d-renderer: a G-buffer at art resolution plus one stylisation shader.
keyFindings.detail: Renders at 320×180, with albedo + flags and normal + linear depth MRT. Adds silhouette ink, creases, hue-shifted OKLab ramps, gradient-aware dithering, orphan-pixel clean-up, an OKLab minimax palette (64–80 colours) and camera snapping.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: A reference design if Orbkin later moves the world to an MRT G-buffer. Read its code before implementing edges and palette (licence not stated).

keyFindings.claim: Octopath and HD-2D sprite pixel dimensions are not published. Orbkin's sprite texel heights are probably in range.
keyFindings.detail: No reliable source gives Octopath sprite sizes (Spriters Resource is blocked here). Dead Cells is about 50 px. Orbkin uses people 44 and kin 28–40 texels at 2 px each, and its own docs measure the reference at people 44–50 and kin about 30.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: Measure the target image before changing sizes. Larger final forms (≥48 texels) may add battle presence.

techniques.name: World-space edge pass (silhouette darken + convex highlight)
techniques.why: It makes 3D tiers, ledges and stairs read as drawn pixel art (t3ssel8r). Orbkin only outlines sprites today.
techniques.how: At 640×360, reconstruct view position from the composer's depth texture, test 4 neighbours, darken the nearer pixel on a depth jump (threshold ∝ linear depth), and brighten the pixel on a convex ridge (positive second difference) by about 1.15–1.25×. Run before sprite compositing; A/B with ?post=edges.

techniques.name: Author arena kit pieces in Blender (glTF)
techniques.why: Hand-coded boxes are the root of the voxel/Minecraft read. HD-2D games use authored low-poly geometry.
techniques.how: 20–40 modular pieces per biome, vertices on a TEXEL grid, one texel density, UVs to an atlas painted by hand or by the existing TS painters; load glTF and merge per material into the existing VoxelBatch-style draw budget.
techniques.effort: 1–2 weeks for the cave set, then about 3–5 days per biome

techniques.name: Authored creature models with the existing live toon bake
techniques.why: Designed silhouettes beat primitive-built bodies, and the live bake keeps all procedural animation hooks.
techniques.how: Blender low-poly (300–1500 tris) with vertex colours or a small palette texture and a simple armature, exported to glTF and fed to SpriteBaker.

techniques.name: Pre-rendered albedo + normal sprite sheets (Dead Cells pipeline)
techniques.why: Allows per-pixel hand clean-up (faces, eyes, hands) while keeping dynamic light.
techniques.how: Headless bpy: ortho camera, 1 spp Cycles emission overrides for albedo and camera-space normal, filter_width 0.01 BOX, film_transparent, Standard view transform; post-outline and palette-protect in numpy; Pixelorama clean-up; billboard with MeshLambertMaterial(map, normalMap, alphaTest) plus banded quantisation via onBeforeCompile.
techniques.effort: about 1 day for the pipeline, then mostly artist time per sheet

techniques.name: Texel-snapped camera with sub-pixel remainder re-applied at upscale
techniques.why: Removes texel crawl while keeping slow camera moves smooth (exact only at the focus depth for a perspective camera).
techniques.how: Round the view offset to whole internal px (already done) and pass the dropped fraction to a final device-resolution sharp-bilinear blit as a UV offset (bababuyyy SharpUpscale).

techniques.name: Sharp-bilinear final upscale
techniques.why: Uniform texel widths at non-integer scales (phones) without blur.
techniques.how: fw = fwidth(uv)/px; grid = uv/px - 0.5*fw; blend = smoothstep(1-fw, 1, fract(grid)); uv' = (floor(grid)+0.5+blend)*px with linear sampling.

techniques.name: Depth-based DOF on the far set only
techniques.why: DOF is central to the HD-2D diorama read, and screen-Y tilt-shift blurs the floor texture.
techniques.how: Blur radius from linear depth beyond the battle focus plane, ≤2 px at 640×360, then Bayer dither; floor, kin and trainers stay sharp.

techniques.name: Palette lock via LUTPass
techniques.why: Grading and bloom drift colours off the authored ramps, while pixel art keeps a fixed palette.
techniques.how: Build a 32³ LUT mapping to the nearest OKLab entry of the arena palette and apply it after the grade, before the dither, at intensity about 0.6; exclude emissive and FX through intensity.

techniques.name: Banded key light on world materials
techniques.why: Quantised light steps are a core pixel-art cue (t3ssel8r, bababuyyy _Cuts=3).
techniques.how: onBeforeCompile on the world Lambert material: band the key N·L (2–3 steps) with a 4×4 Bayer offset before the step; keep the hemisphere fill smooth; keep the shadow map.

techniques.name: Stepped animation playback
techniques.why: 8–12 fps poses read as sprite animation; 60 fps vertex motion reads as a 3D model.
techniques.how: Quantise rig time for idle and ambient motion; keep hit and lunge tweens snappy and texel-quantised.

techniques.name: VFX point lights casting sprite shadows (Octopath)
techniques.why: Grounds FX and sprites in the 3D world; this is a documented Octopath technique.
techniques.how: Spawn a short-lived PointLight at each move impact (shadow-casting on the high tier only, else none), tinted by element, tweened intensity.

techniques.name: Protected palette reduction for baked sprites
techniques.why: Median cut drops small accent colours (verified).
techniques.how: Reuse Orbkin's extractPalette (rare-but-distinct kept) or OKLab minimax merging; never use plain median cut.

techniques.name: Post outline instead of Freestyle for sprites under ~96 px
techniques.why: Freestyle is anti-aliased and clutters small sprites (verified).
techniques.how: 4-neighbour alpha edge set to about 25–30% of the neighbour colour, plus inner contours from normal jumps (1 - n·n' > 0.35) darkened to about 0.55×.
techniques.effort: already in Orbkin's live bake; about 0.5 day for the offline path

techniques.name: Headless Blender asset pipeline in the repo
techniques.why: Reproducible content builds with no GUI or GPU, in CI or this container.
techniques.how: tools/blender/*.py run via pip-installed bpy: glTF import/export, texel-density and palette checks, contact sheets, sprite bakes (scripts in the notes, section 6).

techniques.name: Pre-rendered painted backdrops
techniques.why: Distant vistas do not need live geometry, and a curated pixel painting looks better.
techniques.how: Render a wide Cycles view of a Blender backdrop scene, palette-quantise it, hand-touch it, and place it on a far plane (Orbkin already has backdrop planes).

openQuestions: What are the real pixel dimensions of Octopath / Triangle Strategy character sprites, and their texel-to-screen ratio? (Spriters Resource is blocked here.)
Does the target fan-art's rock use pixel textures on 3D geometry or a painted backdrop? Measure texel density on the reference image against its sprite texels.
What does the depth-reconstructed edge pass cost on a real phone GPU (SwiftShader timings are not representative)?
Why do multi-sample Cycles renders keep fractional alpha with filter_width 0.01 and use_pixel_jitter False in Blender 5.2? (The 1-spp emission passes sidestep it.)
Does Blender's Line Art (Grease Pencil) give crisp 1-px lines at sprite scale? (Not tested.)
Does Sea of Stars use sprite normal maps or another lighting method? (No primary source found.)
How much per-frame hand clean-up can the owner afford, which decides whether P2 stops at authored models with a live bake?
What licence does CelestialLemon/pixel3d-renderer use? Check before reusing code.
